issues.explanation: The dashboard is a Livewire component protected by the custom current_entity middleware, but the application never calls Livewire::addPersistentMiddleware() for it, so the tenant/authorization middleware silently stops applying on /livewire/update requests (Livewire security policy rule 6).

Entity creation is a domain write performed directly in the Livewire component instead of in an app/Actions/* class as the project's Actions convention requires, although the submit()/uniqueSlug() contract makes the retry loop belong in the component.
The same 'Entities and tenancy' entry is added under [Unreleased] (line 12) and again under the already-released [0.0.0] - 2026-07-07 section, misrepresenting the release history.
The audit assertions check only the MessageLogged message and context, never the channel, so the task requirement to log on the audit channel is not actually verified.
The only #[Locked] server context, Dashboard::$entity, has no tamper test, although the Livewire definition of done requires a tamper attempt on locked values.
The guest and unverified redirect tests omit /home, and the switcher title is never asserted as a <title> (the assertion matches the heading string), so those two requirements are not covered.
auditEntries() is defined but never used, leaving dead code in the test suite.
The docblocks say the middleware is the only place that reads current_entity_id, but EntityController::switcher also reads it at app/Http/Controllers/EntityController.php:38.
The zero/one/many membership dispatch is duplicated in the controller and the middleware, so a change to the rule must be made in two places.

review.summary: The change implements the entity/membership model, policies, tenant middleware, /home dispatch, audit-logged entity pick, onboarding with slug retry, dashboard, switcher, navbar entry and extensive tests/docs. Requirements and authorization are essentially complete, but the custom current_entity middleware is not persisted for Livewire updates (a non-negotiable Livewire policy item), the CHANGELOG repeats an entry under [0.0.0], and tests/docs still have minor gaps, so a small round of changes is needed before merging.
